qua: in the role or character of
quarterly forecast: a prediction of results for the next three months
quarterly report: a company's results published every three months
raise an issue: to bring a problem up for people to discuss
reach an agreement: for two sides to finally accept the same terms
read a book: to go through a book and take in its words
read between the lines: to understand what is meant but not said
reduce / diminish / decrease: to make or become smaller in size or amount
rely on: to need someone or something and trust them to work
renewable energy: power from sources such as sun and wind that do not run out
resit: to take an exam again after failing it
restructuring: a major change to the way a company is organized
roadmap: a plan showing the steps and dates of a project
room service: food and drink brought to your hotel room
rub someone up the wrong way: to annoy someone without meaning to
rule of thumb: a rough guide based on practice rather than exact rules
rule out: to decide that something is impossible or unsuitable
run a business: to manage a company and its daily work
run a risk: to do something that could bring trouble
run out of: to use all of something and have none left
sad / unhappy / miserable: feeling low, from quiet sadness to deep misery
sandals: light open shoes held on by straps
say / state / express: to put something into words, plainly, formally, or as a feeling
screen time: the time spent looking at a phone, computer or television
screenshot: a picture of what is showing on a screen
sea level: the height of the sea's surface, used to measure land and air
seat belt: the strap that holds you in your seat in a vehicle
security check: the inspection of people and bags before boarding or entering
see / observe / notice: to use your eyes, to watch carefully, or to become aware
self-care: the things you do to keep yourself healthy and calm
set a goal: to decide what you want to achieve
set an alarm: to make a clock ring at a chosen time
set an example: to behave in a way others should copy
set the record straight: to correct a wrong belief about what happened
set up: to start a business or system, or to arrange equipment
settle out of court: to agree a solution without going to trial
she: the girl or woman being spoken about
show / reveal / disclose: to let something be seen or known
show up: to arrive at a place, often unexpectedly
side effect: an unwanted result of a medicine or action
sign off: to give final approval, or to end a message
sign up: to join a course, service or activity
single room: a hotel room for one person
single-use plastic: plastic made to be thrown away after one use
sit on the fence: to avoid choosing one side in a disagreement
sit on your hands: to do nothing when you should act
slow / gradual / sluggish: not fast, or slower than it should be
small / little / tiny: not large, from small down to very small
smartphone: a phone that runs apps and connects to the internet
smoke alarm: a device that sounds when smoke is in the air
so far so good: everything has gone well up to now
solve a problem: to find a way to fix a difficulty
something: a thing that is not named or known
sort out: to deal with a problem or organize something
sparkling water: water with bubbles of gas in it
speak of the devil: said when the person you were talking about arrives
speak volumes: to show a great deal without words
spend / invest / squander: to use money, wisely, for a return, or wastefully
split the bill: for each person to pay their share of a meal
stand out: to be much more noticeable than those around you
stand the test of time: to stay good or true for a long time
still water: water with no gas bubbles in it
strange / odd / peculiar: unusual in a way that surprises you
strong coffee: coffee made with a lot of ground coffee, so it tastes intense
strong opinion: a view you hold firmly and defend
swallow your pride: to accept something humiliating in order to move on
